blocks.content: Soil texture is a basic permanent physical property of soil, whereas soil structure can be modified through cultivation and management practices.

rows: Relative percentage of sand, silt, and clay particles
Arrangement of primary soil particles into peds or aggregates
Dynamic property (easily changed by tillage and management)
12 classes defined by the Textural Triangle
Categorized by shape: Platy, Prismatic, Blocky, and Granular
Determines inherent water holding capacity and nutrient retention
Determines soil aeration, water infiltration rate, and root penetration

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Soil texture denotes the relative proportion of sand, silt, and clay particles in a given soil mass.
Soil structure defines the spatial arrangement of primary soil particles into aggregated units called peds.
Stokes' Law forms the governing physical principle for mechanical analysis and soil particle size determination.
Soil texture remains virtually permanent, while soil structure is dynamic and easily altered by agricultural management.
Granular and crumb structures provide optimum aeration, drainage, and root penetration for field crops.
ISSS Particle Classification limits: Clay (<0.002 mm), Fine Sand (0.02–0.2 mm), and Coarse Sand (0.2–2.0 mm) are frequently tested in match-the-following questions.
Stokes' Law application: Sedimentation analysis assumes smooth, spherical particles falling in an infinite fluid without turbulence.
Granular and Crumb structural types are considered best for agricultural production, whereas Platy structure restricts water percolation and root development.
